lines.text: This is Sketch2Sim, built today at MLH Hacktoberfest Hack Day Batam.

captions.text: This is Sketch2Sim, built today at MLH Hacktoberfest
Hack Day Batam.

lines.text: Every hardware idea starts as a sketch on paper. Turning that sketch into a working circuit is the slow part: picking pins, adding resistors, writing firmware, and then hunting for the one wire you put in backwards.

captions.text: Every hardware idea starts as a sketch on paper.
Turning that sketch into a working circuit is
the slow part: picking pins,
adding resistors, writing firmware,
and then hunting for the one wire you
put in backwards.

lines.text: So we asked a simple question. What if the sketch was the source code?

captions.text: So we asked a simple question.
What if the sketch was the source code?

lines.text: Draw your circuit right in the browser, or just snap a photo of your notebook, and hit compile.

captions.text: Draw your circuit right in the browser,
or just snap a photo of your notebook,
and hit compile.

lines.text: Gemma 4 reads the drawing. The boxes, the lines, even the handwritten notes. And it returns a complete circuit: the parts, the wiring with a reason for every pin, and the Arduino firmware.

captions.text: Gemma 4 reads the drawing.
The boxes, the lines,
even the handwritten notes.
And it returns a complete circuit:
the parts, the wiring with a reason for

lines.text: But we don't trust the model blindly. Every answer goes through a deterministic validator. It locks each part to a real Wokwi component, fixes pin names, adds missing resistors, and flips parts that are wired backwards. And it shows you every repair it made.

captions.text: But we don't trust the model blindly.

lines.text: Now paste both files into Wokwi, a real circuit simulator, and press play. The traffic light from a pencil sketch is running.

captions.text: Now paste both files into Wokwi,
a real circuit simulator,

lines.text: Five hand-drawn sketches. Five circuits running in Wokwi. We cut compile time from about a hundred seconds to thirty. And if the network drops on stage, presets fall back to a saved run, clearly labeled as cached.
